judgments.justification: Both describe the same Assyrian deportation of Israel (1 Chr 5:26, 2 Kgs 17:6) — near-synonyms, no clear hierarchy in the evidence.
Colour is a descriptive property applied across many materials; Eccl 9:8/Esth 8:15 show color terms modifying linen garments, not one subsuming the other.
Linen is one material dress was made from (2 Sam 6:14's linen ephod) — a composition relation the fixed vocabulary has no clean slot for.

Music,Instrumental is explicitly the instrumental subcategory of the general Music entry (its own definition catalogs specific instruments), and 1 Chr 25:1/1 Sam 10:5 show instrumental performance as one mode of the broader musical practice.
1 Kings 21:27 and 2 Sam 1:12 both show fasting arising as an expression of grief/mourning ('mourned and wept and fasted... for Saul and Jonathan'), not the reverse.
1 Sam 18:6 and Ps 150:4 show dance and instrumental music performed together, not one subsuming the other.
2 Sam 1:24 and Judg 5:30 show color terms describing garments — descriptive-property relation, not hierarchy.
Exod 29:40/Num 15:7 confirm wine as the drink-offering's material — a composition relation outside the fixed vocabulary.
1 Kings 15:13/Deut 7:5 show idols as the object of idolatrous worship — object-to-practice, not a taxonomic subtype.
Exod 16:10 shows the cloud as the visible form the Shechinah (divine presence) took — a symbol-of relation the fixed vocabulary doesn't cover; associated is the honest fallback.

Easton's own Teman entry calls it 'a grandson of Esau, one of the dukes of Edom' and 'a place in Southern Idumea' — a sub-clan/sub-region of Edom, confirmed by Ezek 25:13/Amos 1:12 naming Teman within judgment oracles on Edom.

Easton's Divination entry lists necromancers (who use a familiar spirit) as one of several named methods of divination; 1 Sam 28:8 shows Saul consulting a familiar spirit specifically as an act of divination.
Easton's own Pentecost entry calls it 'the day of the firstfruits' (Exod 34:22) — a specific festival occasion built on the broader first-fruits principle.
Easton's own definitions describe both as near-equivalent tribal/military standards (translating different Hebrew words, 'oth and nes); Isa 11:12/18:3 use them interchangeably.

Cornet (shophar) is one specific instrument; Music,Instrumental's own entry catalogs it alongside harp and psaltery, confirmed by 1 Chr 15:28/13:8 listing it among other named instruments in the same performance.
Easton's own Lamp entry calls it 'that part of the candle-sticks... which bore the light' — a part-of relation the fixed vocabulary doesn't cover.
Both entries describe the same OT clothing practices (tunic, girdle) in near-synonymous terms; 1 Sam 18:4/Gen 41:42 don't distinguish them.
1 Sam 6:2 pairs 'priests and diviners'; Exod 7:11 shows the Egyptian magicians' 'enchantments' as one specific technique of the broader divination practice Easton's Divination entry catalogs.
1 Chr 13:8/1 Sam 10:5 list cymbals among other named instruments as one member of the instrumental-music class Easton's Music,Instrumental entry catalogs.
Exod 28:15/28:4 describe the priestly girdle's coloring — descriptive property, not hierarchy.
Easton's own Edom entry says the land 'was called... the mountain of Seir' — an alternate name for the same territory, not a sub-region.
Deut 32:14 and Gen 49:11 list milk and wine together as coordinate products of agricultural blessing, not one subsuming the other.
Isa 44:3's 'I will pour water on him who is thirsty, streams on the dry ground' directly ties rain/water to growth; Hos 6:3's harvest-rain imagery reinforces rain as agriculture's precondition.
Ezek 31:3/Zech 11:2 treat the cedar as a species of tree named among others in a forest setting — a member of the broader forest-tree category.
1 Chr 11:22/1 Kgs 1:8 list both as contemporaneous royal officials under David — co-occurrence, not hierarchy or causation.
Jer 36:2/36:6 use 'scroll' (roll) and the act of writing/reading a 'book' interchangeably for the same physical object — near-synonyms, not hierarchy.
1 Sam 28:8/Isa 8:19 show a wizard as a practitioner of divination — a person-to-practice relation the fixed vocabulary doesn't cover as cleanly as broader/narrower.
Isa 13:22/34:13 list dragon and owl together among creatures haunting ruined cities — coordinate list items, not hierarchy.
2 Sam 20:23 places Benaiah over the Pelethites as a military unit he commanded — an office-over-unit relation, not a taxonomic one.
Same 2 Sam 20:23 passage: Benaiah commanded the Cherethites alongside the Pelethites — co-occurrence in one administrative list.
1 Chr 6:53/2 Sam 8:17 record Ahimaaz as Zadok's son — a genealogical relation, not broader/narrower/causal in the sense this vocabulary targets.
2 Sam 21:19/1 Chr 20:5 name Goliath specifically within a family/line of Philistine giants — Goliath is a specific instance of the broader Giants category.
Exod 29:40/Num 15:7 list oil and wine together as parallel components of the same offering, not one subsuming the other.
1 Kings 21:27/2 Sam 3:31 show torn clothes and sackcloth as an expression accompanying mourning — associated practices, not hierarchy.
Ezek 16:10/Isa 61:3 mention dress and head ornamentation together descriptively; head-dress is a part of an outfit, a composition relation outside the fixed vocabulary.
1 Sam 18:4/Gen 41:42 don't establish linen specifically as the girdle's material in the cited evidence — kept as co-occurrence rather than asserting a composition the verses don't confirm.
Exod 39:28/Ezek 44:18 explicitly name linen as the head-dress's material — a composition relation the fixed vocabulary doesn't cover; associated is the honest fallback.
Exod 29:13/Lev 9:19 discuss sacrificial fat portions without establishing a taxonomic fat-is-a-food relation stronger than general co-occurrence in offering law.
Lev 23:17/23:10 place the first-fruits wave-offering on the day after the Passover Sabbath — a sequential/calendrical relation, not hierarchy.
Deut 23:19/Ps 15:5 treat usury as interest charged on a loan — a practice conducted via loans, not a taxonomic subtype of Loan.
Exod 22:29/23:19 name firstfruits among general harvest/food offerings without a clean hierarchy in the cited text.
Exod 39:27/Isa 61:10 don't tie colour specifically to head-dress beyond general priestly-garment description — weak co-occurrence, correctly left as associated.
Exod 29:13/Lev 7:3 both specify 'the fat that covers the entrails' (the caul) as one named fat-portion among several in the sacrificial law — a specific fat structure, narrower than fat generally.
Exod 29:13/29:22 describe fat covering the liver — adjacent anatomical parts, not one subsuming the other.
1 Kings 18:38/Lev 9:24 show fire, like the cloud, as a visible form the divine presence (Shechinah) took — a symbol-of relation the fixed vocabulary doesn't cover.
Isa 40:19/Judg 17:4 both describe the physical craft (casting, overlaying with gold/silver) that produces the idol object — the graving process results in the idol existing.
Jer 2:20/Ezek 16:31 use 'harlot' as a designation for one who commits fornication in the prophetic marriage-metaphor — near-synonymous roles, not hierarchy.
2 Sam 5:11/1 Chr 14:1 show Hiram as the supplier of cedar timber to David — a provider-resource relation, not hierarchy.

2 Chr 36:10/36:7 describe the temple's vessels being carried to Babylon during the captivity — historical co-occurrence; calling the captivity a cause of the Temple concept itself would overreach what these verses establish.
Gen 1:11/2:5 name grass and herbs as parallel, coordinate categories of vegetation in the creation account, not one subsuming the other.
